groups.title: North Carolina, 1824–1851
groups.lede: Ashe County, North Carolina. The papers by which the Carson brothers, emigrants from County Antrim, declared their intention to become United States citizens and were naturalized. David Carson’s own citizenship, completed in Missouri in 1844, is the fact on which his 1850 Oregon land claim rested.

groups.title: Oregon probate, 1852–1857
groups.lede: The administration of David Carson’s estate in the Probate Court of Benton County, Oregon Territory, from Greenberry Smith’s appointment as administrator in November 1852 to the confirmation of the land sale in 1857: the bond, the inventory and appraisal, the sale bill, the receipts and billings that passed through the administrator’s hands, and his final accounting.

groups.title: Missouri probate, 1852–1859
groups.lede: The parallel administration in Platte County, Missouri, where David Carson still held land: John Robinson’s settlements, and the powers of attorney by which the Carson heirs in North Carolina, Virginia and Missouri collected their shares. The children Letitia bore in Oregon are not among them.

groups.title: Carson v. Smith, 1854–1857
groups.lede: The two suits Letitia Carson brought against Greenberry Smith in the District Court of Benton County — the first for the value of her labour, the second for cattle — pleaded for her by A. J. Thayer against John Kelsay. The file runs from the February 1854 complaint through the 1855 and 1856 judgments to the receipts of June 1857.

groups.title: Douglas County, 1853–1922
groups.lede: Letitia Carson’s homestead on South Myrtle Creek — the 1863 application and affidavits, the 1868 proof and certificate, the 1869 patent — with her daughter Martha’s 1868 marriage record and the 1884 deed by which Letitia conveyed the land to her son, ending with the 1922 probate of his estate.

groups.title: Myrtle Creek, 2023–2024
groups.lede: Present-day Douglas County assessor records for the ground the homestead stood on, gathered by the creator in 2023 and 2024.
groups.restriction_note: These are current Douglas County assessor records — parcel maps and tax-lot cards for land that is now in other people’s hands. The Library names the folder, counts it and points at the creator’s copy, and does not reproduce present-day parcel detail about private property. The rest of the Myrtle Creek record is in the Douglas County group above.

groups.title: File endorsements and superseded scans
groups.lede: Docket endorsements — the folded outside of a court paper, on which the clerk wrote what was inside — together with a family record and a few scans the creator has replaced elsewhere. Kept because a reader working from the original files will meet them.
